# Wicket Oat

> A themeable UI component library for Apache Wicket 10 (Java 17+), built on the Oat CSS library. Components are plain Wicket components: Java objects bound to models, each attached to a tag in the page's HTML by `wicket:id`, rendered on the server. Not React, not Thymeleaf, not Bootstrap.

These docs describe Wicket Oat 0.6.0 (`dev.jbaby:wicket-oat-core:0.6.0`), for Apache Wicket 10. The links point at the files of that release's tag.

## Rules agents most often get wrong

- Wicket Oat components are Apache Wicket components: Java objects bound to models, each attached to a tag in the page's HTML by `wicket:id` and rendered on the server. Do not write React, Thymeleaf or JSP.
- Call `WicketOats.install(this)` in `WebApplication.init()`. Pages extend `OatAppLayout` (sidebar and top bar) or `OatMobileLayout`, or put `new OatHtml("html")` on `<html wicket:id="html">`.
- Give each component the tag its reference entry names (`OatButton` on `<a>` or `<button>`). Most components bring their own inner markup, so the tag stays empty: `<a wicket:id="save"></a>`.
- Use the lambda factories instead of anonymous subclasses: `OatButton.onClick(id, label, target -> ...)`, `OatSubmitButton.onSubmit(id, label, target -> ...)`. `OatButton` never submits a form; `OatSubmitButton` does.
- Put a `CompoundPropertyModel` on the form; Oat fields take their model and their label (from the page's `.properties` file) by id. After an Ajax submit the fields show and clear their own errors, so don't add `target.add(form)`.
- Show messages with Wicket's `success(...)`/`error(...)` and `Oat.Behaviors.feedbackToasts()` on the page or an `OatFeedbackPanel`; `Oat.toast(target, ...)` is for a one-off toast.
- Style with semantic HTML and Oat's own classes only (`hstack`, `vstack`, `gap-2`, `mt-4`, `row`, `col-6`); never Bootstrap or Tailwind classes. `Oat.Behaviors` styles any Wicket component (`button()`, `badge(OatVariant.SUCCESS)`, `card()`).
- Write no inline styles, `<script>` blocks or `on*` handlers: Wicket's strict Content-Security-Policy stays on. Put CSS in the application's stylesheet, using Oat's variables (`var(--space-4)`, `var(--primary)`).
- An icon-only button needs an `aria-label` or a labelled `OatIcon`.
- Render every changed page in a `WicketTester` test (`tester.startPage(MyPage.class)`): Wicket fails when a `wicket:id` is missing from the markup or from the Java.

## Docs

- [User guide (README)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/v0.6.0/README.md): Installing, the app shell, every component with examples, forms, data tables, CRUD, charts, theming, the Content Security Policy, translations and testing.
- [Components reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/references/components.md): Every component and form field, with its constructors and factories, its options and the markup it needs.
- [Behaviors reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/references/behaviors.md): `Oat.Behaviors`, Oat's styling for any Wicket component.
- [Theming reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/references/theming.md): The 19 built-in themes, switching themes, custom themes and density.
- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/SKILL.md): The skill for Claude Code and other agents that load skills: setup, layout classes, forms and toasts.
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/v0.6.0/CHANGELOG.md): What changed in each release, and how to upgrade.

## Optional

- [All docs in one file](https://danielbartl.github.io/wicket-oat/llms-full.txt): The user guide, the skill and its three references, in this order.
- [Javadoc](https://javadoc.io/doc/dev.jbaby/wicket-oat-core/0.6.0): The API of every class.
- [Examples app source](https://github.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/tree/v0.6.0/wicket-oat-examples): Whole pages built with Wicket Oat: a CRUD table, a customer page, reports, an inbox, a wizard and a phone app. It runs as the [live demo](https://wicket-oat-production.up.railway.app/).
